name: Dione from Voyager 1, November 12, 1980
blurb: Saturn's moon Dione, about 1,120 kilometers across. Seen by Voyager 1's narrow-angle camera through orange, green, blue and violet filters: visible light only, 0.40 to 0.62 µm.
story: The whole of Dione, fully lit, from about 690,000 kilometers away, 11 hours before Voyager 1's closest approach to Saturn on November 12, 1980. Its bright wispy streaks turned out, when Cassini flew past in 2005, to be walls of ice along canyons.
